title: Text Justification
description:
# Text Justification

Given an array of words and an integer `maxWidth`, format the words into lines where every returned string has exactly `maxWidth` characters.

Build each line greedily: starting from the next unused word, place as many words as possible while keeping at least one space between adjacent words. Then render that line using these rules:

* For a normal line with at least two words, distribute all required spaces across the gaps as evenly as possible.
* If the spaces do not divide evenly, earlier gaps on the left receive one more space than later gaps.
* A line with only one word is left-justified: the word is followed by spaces until the line reaches `maxWidth`.
* The final line is also left-justified: words are separated by a single space, then trailing spaces are appended.

Do not remove or reorder words. Spaces inserted by your algorithm are the only spaces in the output lines.

## Example 1:

**Input:** words = ["This", "is", "an", "example", "of", "text", "justification."], maxWidth = 16
**Output:** ["This    is    an","example  of text","justification.  "]

## Example 2:

**Input:** words = ["What","must","be","acknowledgment","shall","be"], maxWidth = 16
**Output:** ["What   must   be","acknowledgment  ","shall be        "]

## Example 3:

**Input:** words = ["Science","is","what","we","understand","well","enough","to","explain","to","a","computer.","Art","is","everything","else","we","do"], maxWidth = 20
**Output:** ["Science  is  what we","understand      well","enough to explain to","a computer.  Art is ","everything  else  we","do                  "]

## Constraints:

* `1 <= words.length <= 300`
* `1 <= words[i].length <= 20`
* `words[i]` consists of non-space English letters and symbols.
* `1 <= maxWidth <= 100`
* `words[i].length <= maxWidth`

examples.output: ["Science  is  what we","understand      well","enough to explain to","a computer.  Art is ","everything  else  we","do                  "]

solutions.name: Greedy Line Packing
solutions.description:
## Approach

Walk through `words` with a start index. For each line, greedily advance the end index while the current words plus the mandatory one-space gaps still fit. Then render that range immediately, either as a left-justified line or as a fully justified line.

## Key Insight

The packing test uses `letters + words[end].length() + (end - start) <= maxWidth`: `(end - start)` is exactly the number of minimum gaps needed if the new word is included. Once the range is fixed, full justification only needs `maxWidth - letters` spaces distributed over `gaps` slots.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n * maxWidth)
- Space Complexity: O(maxWidth) besides the returned lines

solutions.name: Explicit Gap Array Construction
solutions.description:
## Approach

After greedily choosing a line range, compute an integer array where each entry is the exact width of one gap. The rendering loop then only appends a word followed by the already computed number of spaces.

## Key Insight

The gap array separates arithmetic from string construction. Normal lines fill all gaps with `totalSpaces / gaps`, then add one more space to the first `totalSpaces % gaps` gaps, which directly encodes the left-heavy rule.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n * maxWidth)
- Space Complexity: O(maxWidth)

solutions.name: Fixed Width Character Buffer
solutions.description:
## Approach

Allocate a `char[]` of length `maxWidth` for each output line and pre-fill it with spaces. Copy every word into its final position, advancing the write cursor by the computed gap width instead of appending spaces one by one.

## Key Insight

A fixed-width buffer makes the line length invariant automatic. The algorithm still uses the same greedy grouping and left-heavy gap arithmetic, but trailing padding is already present because the buffer starts filled with spaces.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n * maxWidth)
- Space Complexity: O(maxWidth)

solutions.name: Two-Phase Range Rendering
solutions.description:
## Approach

First compute all greedy line ranges and the total letters in each range. Then render each saved range with a helper that knows whether it is the final line. This separates the grouping decision from the formatting decision.

## Key Insight

Saving ranges is useful for teaching and testing because the greedy partition becomes explicit. Once the partition is fixed, every line renderer follows the same formula: last or single-word lines get single internal spaces plus right padding; other lines divide `maxWidth - letters` across the gaps.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n * maxWidth)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
